text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - December Bunds close DTB trade firmer after setting new contract high at 99.30, buoyed by gains in U.S. Treasuries. German markets closed on Thursday for holiday. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.25, up 0.27 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilt futures soared on Wednesday, helped by bullish sentiment in bond markets across the globe but outperforming sharply nonetheless. The December gilt future settled 30/32 higher at 110-02 and dealers said buying at the ultra-long end of the market suggested renewed interest in the UK market. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-02/32, up 30/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - December bond future carried to new contract high in generally bullish market. December PIBOR settles at contract high. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 125.34, up 0.26 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt futures soared ahead in late afternoon with the LIFFE BTP December contract closing at 123.35, just two basis points below the contract. A wave of euphoria over Italy's prospects of joining EMU swept all before it, with the lira rising to 992.80, its highest level since end-July 1994. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 123.30 up 1.35 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries at session highs after construction spending report shows Aug spending +0.9 pct vs. revised -1.1 in July. Construction spending near consensus forecast of +0.8 pct. Market again testing 6.0 pct level on two-year note. 10-yr Treasury note auction terms to be set in afternoon.The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-12/32, up 15/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.48 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond futures ended unchanged after recouping earlier losses in a market that lacked fresh factors. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 122.14, down 0.09 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market volumes continued unabated, with European currencies dominating but dollar issues also surfacing. Two more lira zero-coupon bonds were launched, following a 1.0 trillion lire EIB 15-year deal last week. The World Bank set a 1.0 trillion lire 20-year bond at a 21.294 reoffer price.
